title: Rav Nachman bar Shmuel bar Nachman or Nachmani
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Rav Nachman bar Shmuel bar Nachman (or Nachmani). Hyman says he learned from his father and transmitted in his name in Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat, chapter 1, end of halakhah 4, and Bereshit Rabbah 9:7. Jerusalem Talmud Bava Batra 9:4 relates that he was seized for the king’s service, and the case came before R’ Ami.

Tanchuma Buber, Noach 24, gives the name R’ Nechemyah. Hyman says it SHOULD READ Nachman, as in the old Tanchuma. At the beginning of Tetzaveh, Hyman finds Rav Nachman bar Shmuel and says that the words “bar Nachmani” are missing.
At the end of Jerusalem Talmud Megillah 1:1 he answers R’ Chelbo.

In his quotation from Kohelet Rabbah 2:24, Hyman gives the names Rabbi Tanchuma, Rabbi Nachman son of Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachman, and Rabbi Menachma, with this teaching: “All eating and drinking mentioned in this Scroll refers to Torah and good deeds.”

notes.text: The Kohelet Rabbah attribution has the supplied Tanchuma, Nachman and Menachma sequence; its exact linking syntax remains compressed. The suggested Nechemyah-to-Nachman correction and missing patronymic are Hyman’s own.

The whole saved TE KoheletRabbah 2:24 scalar 0 explicitly names full Rabbi Tanchuma, Rabbi Nachman son of Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachman, and Rabbi Menachma, followed by an alternative Yirmeyah/Meyasha/ShmuelbarRavYitzchak chain absent from Hyman’s short citation. This supports these local name and full-title occurrences without inventing connectors among the compressed first names or importing the omitted alternative into Hyman’s body. Nachman/Nachmani remain variants. Hyman says the Nechemyah form SHOULD READ Nachman; the force, attribution and his missing-patronymic claim remain. There does not establish which Tanchuma edition the next quotation uses. Ami/Chelbo/Nechemyah are uninspected R-prime occurrences, not automatically full Rabbi.

Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 1:4 has Nachmani, and Bereshit Rabbah 9:7 has Rabbi Nachman reporting Rav Shmuel bar Nachman. In Jerusalem Talmud Bava Batra 9:4, the case before Rabbi Immi (Ami) concerns whether the cost of government service comes from Nachman’s own property or the common estate. In Megillah 1:1, Rabbi Chelbo says he never heard this teaching from Shmuel bar Nachman, and Nachman asks whether Chelbo heard everything his father had taught. Buber’s Noach 24 has Nechemyah, while Torat Emet’s Noach 18 has Nachman son of Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani in the parallel parable. The consulted Tetzaveh 1 has Rav Nachman bar Shmuel, and Hyman says bar Nachmani is missing. The Kohelet Rabbah witness preserves the compressed first attribution and goes on to give an alternative chain through Yirmeyah and Meyasha in the name of Shmuel bar Rav Yitzchak.
